claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr forms a homogeneous polycrystalline solid solution.
The high-entropy effect in equimolar WTaTiVZr induces atomic-scale lattice distortion.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion lowers the effective dislocation barrier in WTaTiVZr.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion activates additional slip systems in WTaTiVZr.
Equimolar alloying reduces the critical resolved shear stress in WTaTiVZr.
Additional slip-system activation facilitates dislocation mobility and more effective strain hardening.
WTaTiVZr develops ductile intergranular features that promote dislocation climb and crack blunting.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and strain hardening delay crack nucleation and propagation in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten has more limited slip-system activity than equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten has higher dislocation pinning than equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Under identical high-temperature tensile loading, WTaTiVZr will have significantly greater plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The improved toughness of WTaTiVZr will be manifested as distributed plastic deformation and crack blunting.
The proposed dislocation-mediated mechanism should dominate at high temperatures where dislocation mobility is the primary deformation mode.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at low temperatures.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under irradiation because radiation-induced defects could alter deformation.
Matched grain size, texture, temperature, atmosphere, and strain rate can be used to isolate intrinsic differences between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
A different refractory high-entropy alloy, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 or its nitrogen-doped analogue, can combine approximately 1400 MPa tensile yield strength with approximately 20% ductility.
